description: Infrabel, the Belgian railway infrastructure manager, publishes two datasets on railway traction energy use on its open data portal, read on 2026-09-26. One gives total traction energy consumption per month in MWh since 1987; the other, since 2009, breaks the monthly total down by region and by type of traffic. The descriptions explain that electricity is taken at high voltage to Infrabel's traction substations, transformed and distributed through the catenary, and drawn by train pantographs for traction, lighting, heating and air conditioning. Both datasets were last modified on 5 July 2022 and are free under the CC0 universal licence. Caveats: updates stopped in 2022, and the distributed dataset uses generic column names, so the schema must be read before use. Simulation uses are the electricity demand of rail traction for capacity planning and for studying interdependencies between the power grid and rail networks. Related records: data-sp-energy-networks-open-data-portal gives substation-level load forecasts for comparison.
